subcohort.evidence_quote: Seventeen traveled to Central Africa and 18 to the Indian peninsula
subcohort.notes: Two travel-destination subcohorts defined by the study.

target_condition.evidence_quote: we used explorative shotgun metagenomic sequencing to address the abundance of >300 antibiotic resistance genes in fecal specimens
target_condition.notes: Study is exposure/travel-focused rather than disease-focused; target phenotypes inferred from stated aims (resistome abundance and ESBL acquisition), combined with 'Of 18 students visiting the Indian peninsula, 12 acquired ESBL-producing Escherichia coli' (Abstract).

control.notes: Study design is a self-controlled before/after travel comparison, not a disease case-control study; no explicit case/control labeling given, so 'Not Used' assigned with low confidence.

country.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies were invited to participate
country.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
country.notes: Participants reside in Sweden; fecal specimens self-submitted before departure and after return to Sweden.

body_site.evidence_quote: self-submission of separate fecal specimens for metagenomic analysis and culture screening
body_site.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

days_from_first_collection.evidence_quote: collected at a median of 4 days before departure (range 0 to 23) and 22 days (range 2 to 120) after return to Sweden
days_from_first_collection.notes: Only aggregate median/range collection timing reported; no single per-sample day value derivable without inventing per-sample data.

location.evidence_quote: Seventeen traveled to Central Africa and 18 to the Indian peninsula
location.notes: Represents travel destination, distinct from residence country (Sweden).

westernized.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
westernized.notes: Sweden is a westernized country; not explicitly labeled 'westernized' in text.

sequencing_platform.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_current_use.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Applies to the entire cohort as an inclusion criterion; also stated in Discussion that no antibiotics were taken before or during travel.

disease.notes: Participants are described as health care students without antibiotic use, but no explicit healthy/disease status statement was found.

by_subgroup.Central Africa: All travelers to Central Africa used antimalarial chemoprophylaxis

treatment.evidence_quote: All travelers to Central Africa and 44% (8/18) of travelers to the Indian peninsula used antimalarial chemoprophylaxis.
treatment.notes: Specific agents mefloquine, proguanil, and atovaquone are mentioned in the Discussion as antimalarial agents used by some study subjects; exact per-subject usage rates not fully broken down for each agent.

biomarker_name.notes: These are the three most prominent, statistically significant fold-change increases reported for antibiotic resistance gene categories after travel.

extraction_warnings: Paper reports only cohort-level and destination-stratified aggregate statistics (age range, % female, median collection days, diarrhea rates); no per-subject or per-sample rows are present in the provided text (likely only in supplementary Table S1, not included).
Subject/sample identifiers, DNA extraction kit, and detailed ancestry/family information are not reported in the provided text.
The 'control' field concept (case/control) does not map cleanly onto this before/after travel exposure study; assigned 'Not Used' with low confidence.
target_condition was derived/inferred since the study is exposure-focused (travel) rather than a classic disease case-control study.
Sequencing platform differs for isolate genomes (Illumina MiSeq) versus metagenomic fecal samples (Illumina HiSeq 2000); IlluminaHiSeq was chosen as primary for fecal metagenomic samples.

Paper describes a cohort of 35 healthy Swedish exchange students; most demographic/clinical schema fields (BMI, dietary restriction, disease status, HLA, neonatal, obgyn, smoker, tumor staging) are not applicable/reported in this microbiome-focused travel study.
Age is only reported as a range (23–34 years) for the whole cohort, not per-individual, so age_years and sample-level granularity could not be determined.
Disease status (e.g., 'Healthy') was not explicitly stated, only implied by study design (health care students, no antibiotic use); left as not_reported to avoid fabrication.
Treatment field captures antimalarial chemoprophylaxis usage, which is subgroup-stratified by travel destination (Central Africa vs Indian peninsula).
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('subgroup_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 2 subgroups [] differ from batch 0 ['Central Africa', 'Indian peninsula']; kept batch 0.
This paper is not an oncology/clinical trial study; fields related to disease response, ECOG status, and tumor size are not applicable and were marked not_reported.
The schema's 'feces_phenotype_value' field lacks a paired 'feces_phenotype' category field in this schema instance, making it ambiguous which phenotype values to map; left as not_reported.

Biomarker fields were populated with the three headline antibiotic-resistance-gene fold-change values (sulfonamide, trimethoprim, beta-lactam) as these were the most explicitly quantified and repeatedly emphasized in Abstract, Results, and Discussion; other reported values (e.g., per-16S rRNA gene counts, taxonomic abundances) were not included to avoid overextension beyond clearly parallel list entries.
